rows.title: Stop/activate/wait races tested
rows.evidence: Iteration 4 (delta F5): SharedLifecycle sync core (single lock owns LifecycleState + three-valued GateEffect; every mutation via LifecycleState::apply; CAS+release one critical section). 5 Loom models exhaust interleavings: two activations -> one winner/one release; activate-vs-stop never both-win-and-release; death-vs-stop one fact; no release after SupervisorLost; duplicate cleanup one winner. Harness detects deliberately weakened CAS (3/5 models fail). Gate: RUSTFLAGS=--cfg nono_loom cargo test -p nono --test loom_lifecycle --release. Iteration 6 (delta F7) added scenario 6, so the R05 model set is complete: 7 Loom models. The two new ones cover the durable store's own race - a recovery reconciling a record while another party confirms the same cleanup (exactly one CleanupConfirmed winner; a recovery that observes the cleanup already proven records nothing) and a recovery racing a stop-then-cleanup (never adopt after cleanup). The recovery's read-decide-record is deliberately not one critical section - reconcile() is pure over an already-read state - and these models are what say that gap is safe.

rows.title: Mode-aware fs capability semantics honest
rows.evidence: AccessMode is Read/Write/ReadWrite only (capability.rs:86-93), bundling disclosed in docs/cli/internals/landlock.mdx. macOS exec unconditional ((allow process-exec*) macos.rs:555); atomic-write is CLI regex hack (capability_ext.rs:434-460); unix-socket separately modeled (honest). || Iteration 10 (delta F11) landed the mode vocabulary. crates/nono/src/capability_modes/ defines FsMode over the 13 contract operations (read_contents, read_dir, read_metadata, write, append, create, truncate, remove_file, remove_dir, rename, execute, unix_socket_connect, atomic_write), a Copy bitset FsModeSet, and CapabilitySet::allow_path_modes / allow_file_modes beside the untouched allow_path/allow_file. AccessMode behaviour is unchanged and is now STATED rather than implied by FsModeSet::describes_access_mode, which also names the one residual it cannot express (coarse Linux Write grants six non-regular MAKE_* rights and no FsMode does). atomic_write is a NAMED BUNDLE not magic: FsMode::ATOMIC_WRITE_MEMBERS = {create,write,rename,remove_file} is a published constant, every member it adds beyond the request appears in CompiledModes::bundled, and a member the platform will not express refuses the whole grant (on Landlock V1 that is rename, so atomic_write refuses there). unix_socket_connect does NOT duplicate UnixSocketCapability: naming it registers a real one through the same constructor allow_unix_socket uses and the compile result reports it as DELEGATED. Compilation returns CompiledModes{enforced, bundled:[(requested, also_granted, why)], always_allowed:[(mode,why)], refused:[(mode,why)], delegated:[(mode,target)]} readable before applying via Sandbox::compile_fs_modes(&caps) - the SAME compilation the profile/ruleset is built from, so disclosure and enforcement cannot disagree. bundled lists exactly the modes the caller did NOT ask for that the grant confers anyway, which is the anti-silent-widening guarantee. LINUX: read_contents->READ_FILE, read_dir->READ_DIR, write/append->WRITE_FILE (AppendImpliesWrite disclosed both directions), create->MAKE_REG ONLY (decision: the six other MAKE_* rights are separated out and NOT granted; documented in landlock.mdx and asserted by create_grants_make_reg_and_no_other_node_type), remove_file->REMOVE_FILE, remove_dir->REMOVE_DIR, execute->EXECUTE, truncate->TRUNCATE only at ABI>=3, rename->REFER only at ABI>=2, otherwise typed RefusalReason::UnsupportedRight{right,abi,needed_abi} -> NonoError::ModeUnsupported which FAILS PREPARE/APPLY CLOSED (never dropped: on those kernels the operation is not restrictable at all, so a rule compiled to nothing would read as enforcement). read_metadata CANNOT BE RESTRICTED by Landlock: typed always_allowed disclosure, and the support report marks it unrestrictable. MACOS: read_contents->file-read-data+file-map-executable, read_dir->file-read-data (bundled with read_contents), read_metadata->file-read-metadata (ENFORCEABLE - the one place macOS is finer than Linux), write/append/truncate->file-write-data (bundles disclosed), create->file-write-create, remove_file/remove_dir->file-write-unlink (bundled), rename->the file-write-create + file-write-unlink pair with the composition disclosed, atomic_write->that cluster plus the hex-suffixed temp-sibling rule for file grants, ported WITH ATTRIBUTION from nono-cli/src/capability_ext.rs:434-460 (hex-suffix + read-metadata fix in 5f0b95a0) and narrowed from upstream's file-write* to the four operations a temp write performs. execute FIXES the unconditional (allow process-exec*) at macos.rs:555: that exact line is still emitted for a capability set with NO mode grants (every existing consumer including all of nono-cli, so upstream tests stay byte-identically green) and becomes (allow process-exec* (<filter>)) per execute-granted path as soon as the set carries one mode grant. EVIDENCE - macOS: LIVE-PROVEN, 14 positive/negative lifecycle pairs in crates/nono/tests/lifecycle_modes_live.rs run through real prepare/activate/wait, covering read_contents, read_dir, read_metadata, write, append, create, truncate, remove_file, remove_dir, rename, execute and atomic_write; the macOS-only metadata distinction is proven as two runs against ONE read_metadata grant (stat -f %z exits 0, cat is denied) and the execute refusal is observed as a typed ActivationError::PreExecFailed{stage: Exec, errno: EPERM} with no shell in the way. EVIDENCE - Linux: the mapping LOGIC is host-tested against FAKED rights - landlock_map::compile takes a LandlockRightsAvailable (an ABI number) instead of reading the kernel, so all 10 leaf arms, both ABI gates, the always-allowed disclosure, the delegation and the bundle closure run in the ordinary macOS suite (10 tests). Only access_fs_for, abi_version_number and the two rule loops in sandbox/linux.rs need a kernel; they carry 6 cfg(target_os=linux) tests including one that asserts the pure availability table agrees with landlock::AccessFs::from_all for every right at every ABI, which are WRITTEN-UNVERIFIED behind the R07 Docker blocker. REMOVAL-DETECTION transcripts (all three reverted): (a) deleting the ABI gate (refuse closure -> always None) fails 3 tests, truncate_is_refused_below_abi_v3_rather_than_dropped printing left [] right [ModeRefusal{mode:Truncate, why:UnsupportedRight{right:Truncate, abi:1, needed_abi:3}}]; (b) deleting the Landlock always-allowed arm fails read_metadata_is_a_disclosed_no_op_not_a_grant; (c) restoring the unconditional (allow process-exec*) for mode-built profiles fails the live pair execute_granted_runs_an_unheard_of_program_and_ungranted_is_refused_at_exec with 'activation was expected to fail; the run ended Ok(Exited { code: 0 })'. SupportReport gains fs_modes: a per-mode enforceability table (enforceable / bundled_with{mode} / unrestrictable / needs_abi{abi} / unsupported / delegated{target}), probed_live on Linux against the real detected ABI and platform_api on macOS, partial on BOTH platforms for opposite reasons, with a test that cross-checks every entry against what the compiler actually does so the table cannot drift from the mapping. Schema doc + golden example updated. The row is not PASS only because the Linux half has never run.

rows.title: Detached sessions/attach survive caller restart
rows.evidence: Iteration 6 (delta F7) landed slice A: durable schema-versioned session store + identity-reconciled recovery (ADR-0001 s6), library-level in crates/nono/src/lifecycle/session_store.rs. SessionRecord v1 (schema_version const 1; a newer version is typed UnsupportedSchemaVersion found by a version probe read before the rest of the shape, never a field-by-field guess) carrying session UUIDv7, generation, ProcessIdentity, process group, LifecycleState, optional ActivationObservation, created/updated wall timestamps and a bounded opaque metadata copy - no product concept, no command line, no environment. Storage: 0700 dir created-or-opened and CHECKED not repaired (not-a-symlink / owned by the effective uid / no group-or-world bits, each typed); dir opened once O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW and every record reached by openat against that descriptor so no later operation re-walks the path; records <uuid>.json at 0600 (explicit fchmod over the umask), first write O_EXCL, updates write-to-temp + renameat in the same dir (temp O_EXCL, 0600, randomized, not a record name), fsync file then dir. Corruption is typed SessionCorrupt{path,why} and enumeration yields one Result per record, so a corrupt record is reported BESIDE its healthy siblings rather than hiding them. Durable prepare persists at Prepared after the gate-ready observation and every later transition updates the record outside the sync_core lock - the record can lag the live state by one step, which is documented and is exactly why recovery reconciles. Ephemeral PreparedSandbox::prepare is unchanged (no store, no file). Recovery: pure reconcile(state, verdict) -> RecoveryDecision {AlreadyVerified | ProcessGone{basis} | StillRunning{survivors} | Unsettled{reason} | Unsupported{reason}}; a cleanup_verified record is AlreadyVerified whatever the probe says (never adopt a reissued pid); a record in a watched state is moved to Failed with SupervisorLost and persisted. Honest limitation, reported not papered over: a recovered process is NOT our child, so waitpid cannot reach it and its exit code/signal are unobservable - RecoveredSession has no wait, returns no SandboxExit and has no killing Drop; it offers kill_group/kill_pid (same targets<=1 refusal as stop) and verify_cleanup_by(deadline) polling until ESRCH. Generations stay at 1 (one-shot session UUIDs; increments are reserved for slice B's re-prepare). Proven: 27 new unit tests + 2 live, each guard removal-detected (record O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the symlinked record is followed and the decoy is returned; store-dir O_NOFOLLOW dropped -> the store lands on the link's 0755 target; skip-on-parse-failure -> 4 records become 1; schema check deleted -> a v2 record is read as v1; permission check deleted -> a 0755 store is accepted). Live end-to-end: durable prepare -> a caller that crashes (test-only abandon: gate closed, no kill, no reap) -> fresh SessionStore::open -> the record still says 'prepared' -> recover reconciles it to ProcessGone{PidAbsent} -> verify_cleanup ConfirmedAbsent -> the record reads cleanup_verified. Pending for slice B: detached supervisor that keeps exit facts observable across a restart, attach, and the re-prepare flow that increments generation. Linux verification still blocked (R07). || Iteration 8 (delta F9) landed slice B: the detached supervisor, per docs/adr/0002-detached-supervisor.md. THE MECHANISM, and why it is shaped this way: a library has no binary of its own to re-exec, and forking a LONG-RUNNING supervisor out of a threaded caller is undefined-behaviour territory (allocator locks held by threads that no longer exist; the macOS ObjC runtime aborts outright). ADR-0001's gate child survives fork only because it is syscall-only until execve. So the supervisor is THIS BINARY RE-EXECUTED, opted into by one line of embedder cooperation - nono::lifecycle::supervisor_entry() as the FIRST statement of main(). No-op without a private environment marker (NONO_LIFECYCLE_SUPERVISOR, documented as protocol not configuration, and REMOVED from the environment before any other work so it can never be inherited by a customer child); with the marker it never returns. TWO FORKS, both under ADR-0001 child discipline (syscalls only over parent-built buffers, ending in execve or _exit): the launcher forks an intermediate which forks the supervisor-to-be, writes its pid on the handshake and _exit(0)s - so the supervisor is reparented to init and a long-lived launcher never accumulates a zombie it cannot be expected to reap (this was found by test (g), which could not observe the supervisor's death until the double fork was added); the supervisor-to-be setsid()s, points 0/1/2 at /dev/null, forks the CUSTOMER CHILD through the unchanged child_main, writes a bootstrap blob, clears close-on-exec on its five survivors, sweeps every other descriptor (close_inherited_descriptors extended from a pair to a sorted set), and execve()s. execve replaces an IMAGE and not a PROCESS, so the customer child is still the child of the same pid afterwards - which is the entire reason a detached run's exit facts are directly observable via waitpid. NOTHING ABOUT THE PLAN CROSSES THE EXEC: exec image, argv, environment and platform policy are built and used on the launcher's side, so a CapabilitySet is never serialized and re-trusted across a boundary. SECRETS: the gate release/abort pair travels on a private bootstrap pipe (the customer child already holds it) and is zeroized after parse; the ACTIVATION TOKEN is drawn IN THE SUPERVISOR after the exec and handed back on the readiness handshake, so it never exists in the customer child's address space at all - strictly stronger than the attached path, where it exists between fork and exec. NO BIND RACE: the launcher binds and listens on <store>/<session>.sock (unlink-guarded, 0600 inside the 0700 store, sockaddr_un length REFUSED not truncated) BEFORE the fork and passes the LISTENING descriptor through the exec, so readiness implies a socket that has been listening since before the supervisor existed. Readiness is a byte-tagged handshake carrying the supervisor's own ProcessIdentity and the token, poll-bounded; a binary whose main lacks the hook fails closed at a 20s deadline with PrepareError::SupervisorUnresponsive WHICH NAMES THE FUNCTION. SUPERVISOR LOOP: single-threaded poll over {listening socket, held child's status descriptor, SIGCHLD self-pipe with an errno-preserving handler, connected client}; ONE CLIENT AT A TIME (a second is sent a typed ControlRefusal::Busy and closed, never queued - attach single-client discipline is reserved for slice C); child exit observed by a new ActivatedSandbox::try_wait (waitpid WNOHANG) so a wait never parks the one thread; every transition and the SandboxExit persisted; serving continues after a client detaches; the process exits on CleanupVerified or after IDLE_AFTER_TERMINAL_GRACE (300s, documented on the constant) with a terminal state and nobody connected. PROTOCOL V1 (lifecycle/protocol.rs): u32-LE length-prefixed frames, MAX_CONTROL_FRAME_BYTES = 64 KiB checked FROM THE PREFIX BEFORE A BYTE OF BODY IS READ OR ALLOCATED; hello first in both directions carrying {version, session, generation} each checked on both sides; ops Activate{token[32]} / Wait{deadline_millis} / Stop / Status / VerifyCleanup / Goodbye; replies carry the module's EXISTING typed results (ActivationError, StopError, SandboxExit, CleanupVerification, LifecycleState) rather than rendered strings, which is why ActivationError and StopError gained serde derives; peer-uid checked at accept by REUSING supervisor::socket::peer_credentials (no duplicate mechanism) with a foreign uid closed WITHOUT A WORD, since answering would confirm the session exists; the token is compared supervisor-side by the existing gate digest, never persisted, and redacted from ControlRequest's hand-written Debug. EVERY read and write on BOTH sides is poll-deadline-bounded, closing ADR-0001's unbounded-read residual for this path. CLIENT: DetachedSession::{activate, wait, stop, status, verify_cleanup, detach} - dropping it closes a socket and the run carries on, the opposite of every other handle in the module. RECORD SCHEMA V2 (docs/lifecycle/session-record-v2.md): adds supervisor: Option<ProcessIdentity>, exit: Option<SandboxExit> (witnessed exit facts, durable across a caller restart - the thing slice A could not give), and events: Vec<LifecycleEvent> (bounded ring, DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY = 32, oldest dropped). The ring is the HONEST representation of a real limit: EventSink is caller-side by design, so events observed while nobody is connected are NOT deliverable live and are not pretended to be. V1 COMPATIBILITY IS EXPLICIT, NOT LENIENT: the version probe chooses between two deny_unknown_fields shapes, a v1 record is parsed as v1 and upgraded IN MEMORY (no supervisor, no exit, empty ring - absence reported, never invented), the file is untouched until something writes it, and a version neither shape implements is still UnsupportedSchemaVersion. RECOVERY: reconcile gains a third pure input SupervisorPresence {NeverDetached, Alive, Gone} (fail-closed through ProcessIdentity::is_same_process) and a RecoveryDecision::Attachable that outranks every child probe but NOT AlreadyVerified (a proven cleanup stays terminal); an attachable record is NOT moved to Failed, because the live supervisor owns it and a second writer would be the exact hazard the store exists to avoid; a Gone supervisor's stale socket is unlinked by the store at the point its staleness was established by identity rather than guessed from a failed connect. SUPPORT REPORT: detached_supervisor is now Available/PlatformApi with the entry-hook PRECONDITION spelled out in reason.why_not_probed (a probe would have to launch a supervisor: two forks, an exec, a bound socket and a durable record), and attach is Partial - control attach landed, TERMINAL attach did not. STATED LIMITS, not omissions: a headless detached run's standard streams are /dev/null (a supervisor holding its launcher's pipes is the thing detachment is for; giving output back is slice C's PTY); gate expiry stays lazily evaluated at the next control operation, exactly as on the attached path, so an abandoned never-activated detached session holds its supervisor until the plan's activation_expiry is reached at that next operation. PROVEN: 32 new unit tests + a new harness=false integration target crates/nono/tests/lifecycle_detached.rs (15 live, 1 ignored per R18) whose own main() installs the entry hook - libtest owns main and offers no pre-main hook, and the same main is what makes the core proof possible. THE R09 CORE PROOF (test b): the test binary re-runs ITSELF with a private flag as a launcher, that launcher prepares a detached session, prints the session id and token, and EXITS; the main test process - which forked nothing involved - opens the store, recover() answers Attachable, attach() connects, activate() releases the child with a token that crossed a process boundary, and wait() returns Exited{0}/Observed witnessed by waitpid IN THE SUPERVISOR. Also proven live: activate/wait/verify end to end; exit observed while fully detached and read back after reconnect; stop-before-activation with activation-after-stop refused as a typed AlreadyStopped over the wire; replayed Activate refused as AlreadyActivated by the gate's own state machine (not by the protocol); wrong protocol version, wrong session, wrong generation, oversize frame, garbage frame, operation-before-hello and second-concurrent-client all refused with typed frames and closed; SIGKILLed supervisor leaves a stale socket that recover() removes before falling back to the slice-A cleanup path. REMOVAL-DETECTED: hello version check deleted -> the wrong-version client is GREETED instead of refused; frame-length bound deleted -> the supervisor reads a body that never arrives and the oversize test fails with 'the supervisor must answer'; stale-socket unlink deleted -> 'recovery must remove the stale socket it just proved dead'; hello-first guard deleted -> a Status sent before any hello is served. Every test-side wait is bounded. PENDING FOR SLICE C: PTY ownership and terminal attach/detach/resize on the same socket with a distinct channel discipline (contract 8), and the re-prepare flow that increments generation (still always 1). Linux verification still blocked (R07): the F9 code is platform-neutral apart from the Linux close_range arm of the extended sweep and has not been executed on a Linux kernel by this stream. || Iteration 9 (delta F10) landed slice C: the run's TERMINAL, supervisor-owned, with attach/input/resize/detach/reattach over the same control socket. INTERACTIVE IS A QUESTION OF OWNERSHIP, NOT A FEATURE FLAG: a PTY master has to be held for as long as the run lives, and the ephemeral paths have nothing that outlives the call to hold one - so SessionMode::Interactive is supported on the DETACHED path only and refused everywhere else with the typed PrepareError::InteractiveNeedsSupervisor, which names the method that does implement it (refuse_unsupported now judges interactive exactly as it already judged detachment). ALLOCATION: terminal::open_pty runs in the LAUNCHER before any fork - posix_openpt(O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY), grantpt, unlockpt, open(slave, O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC) - because each of those can allocate, take a lock or walk the filesystem, none of which a forked child may do; what crosses the fork is two descriptor numbers. O_NOFOLLOW is deliberate: the path came from the kernel and names a device node, so a symlink under it would mean something replaced the terminal between unlockpt and the open. macOS has no ptsname_r in libc's Apple declarations and ptsname writes into a static buffer a threaded embedder could be sharing, so the slave name comes from TIOCPTYGNAME (what ptsname_r calls there anyway); libc declares no TIOC* numbers for Apple either, so TIOCSCTTY/TIOCSWINSZ/TIOCPTYGNAME are carried in terminal.rs and a unit test RECOMPUTES all three from the BSD _IOC encoding rule, so a transposed digit fails there rather than as an ENOTTY at the point of use. THE CHILD LEADS A SESSION, NOT A GROUP: TIOCSCTTY is refused for a process that is not a session leader, and a terminal nobody controls delivers no SIGINT, no SIGWINCH and no hangup - so an interactive child calls setsid() where a headless one calls setpgid(0,0). Nothing downstream loses by it: setsid also makes a new process group whose id is the child's own pid, so the group the parent recorded is still the group the run lives in and R11's group probe is unchanged. Child sequence, still syscalls-only to exec: close the parent's ends -> setsid -> dup2(slave,0/1/2) -> TIOCSCTTY with arg 0 (never 1, which STEALS a terminal) -> close the spare slave AND the master (a program holding the master of its own terminal could read back everything it wrote and everything typed at it) -> sandbox apply -> sweep, which keeps nothing extra. The terminal is adopted BEFORE the sandbox apply, so a confined child is never granted the right to open a device node. New typed PreExecStage::ControllingTerminal, wire tag 0x17. MASTER OWNERSHIP, TRACED END TO END: the launcher opens both ends and drops both at the fork (a slave copy left there would keep the terminal open after the run ended, so the supervisor's master would never see the end of output; a master copy would mean two processes could read one run); the intermediate closes the slave after forking the customer and clears close-on-exec on the master so it crosses the execve; the supervisor re-arms close-on-exec, sets O_NONBLOCK, and is the ONLY holder anywhere. close_inherited_descriptors gained a '< 3' skip so the -1 that stands in for 'no terminal' in a fixed-size keeper set (a forked child may not allocate) cannot move the sweep's cursor and close 0/1/2. ATTACH PROTOCOL: ControlRequest::Attach{window} is an ordinary control frame and the ControlReply::AttachAck answering it is the LAST control frame the connection carries; after it both sides speak [u8 tag][u32 LE len][bytes] - Input(0x01)/Output(0x02)/Resize(0x03: rows,cols u16 LE)/Detach(0x04)/SessionEnded(0x05: JSON TerminalEnd)/Ping(0x06)/Pong(0x07) - until a Detach switches them back. RAW AND CONTROL ARE DISTINCT BY FRAMING, NOT CONTENT: an Input payload reaches the master byte for byte including 0xFF, NULs and a sequence that IS a well-formed frame header, because the length prefix already said how many bytes the frame owns; there is no escape to get wrong and no in-band sequence to collide with. Direction is enforced (an Output from a client, an Input from a supervisor, are each a peer claiming to own the other end); the 32 KiB payload bound is checked from the prefix before a byte is buffered; an unknown tag, a wrong-direction tag or an oversize length is a typed AttachViolation and the end of the CHANNEL, never of the run. ControlRefusal::NoTerminal refuses an attach to a headless run rather than seating a client in front of silence. SLOT DISCIPLINE UNCHANGED: attach occupies the one client slot and a second connection still gets ControlRefusal::Busy; there is deliberately no AttachBusy, because a second attach cannot reach the supervisor to be refused. SUPERVISOR LOOP: the master joins the poll set (readable while there is somewhere to put output, writable while a client has typed something the terminal has not taken), and the poll set became a WatchSet carrying each descriptor's meaning - a positional descriptors.get(2) would silently read the terminal's readiness as the client's once the set grew. Output with a client attached becomes Output frames behind a bounded 256 KiB in-flight queue with backpressure to the run and a 10 s stall deadline after which THE CLIENT IS DROPPED AND THE SESSION IS NOT; output with nobody attached goes to a bounded 256 KiB oldest-dropped ring that COUNTS what it dropped, and both counts ride on the next AttachAck. The run's end is a SessionEnded frame carrying the typed SandboxExit, queued only after the pass that drained the master, so everything the program wrote is already in front of it. TWO DEADLOCKS FOUND BY THE LIVE TESTS AND FIXED, BOTH REAL AND BOTH VERIFIED WITH STANDALONE C REPRODUCTIONS BEFORE THE FIX: (1) a session leader holding a controlling terminal CANNOT FINISH EXITING until that terminal's output has drained, and the only process that can drain it is the one about to block in waitpid - measured: waitpid never returns, while draining or closing the master reaps in 10 ms. So Supervisor::stop drains and then HANGS THE TERMINAL UP before the kill, Supervisor::wait services the terminal on every slice (without which a run that outran the tty buffer blocked writing while its own caller waited for it to finish - this is what made the ring-flood test hang), and the loop hangs up before any handle's Drop can reap. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a stopped interactive run may be observed as Signaled{SIGHUP} rather than SIGKILL, and a later attach still works and still replays the ring. (2) macOS killpg answers EPERM, NOT ESRCH, for a process group whose every member is already a zombie, so a stop that raced the run's own exit reported 'the signal could not be delivered' - a pre-existing R11 fragility that only became reachable here. ActivatedSandbox::stop/drop now go through a private kill_own_group which reads EPERM as 'nothing left in the group to signal', and ONLY there, where the group id is an unreaped child's own pid and so cannot have been reissued; RecoveredSession::kill_group deliberately keeps the strict reading because its recorded group id may well have been. CLIENT API: DetachedSession::attach(window) -> AttachedTerminal{write_input, resize, ping, read_event(deadline), activate, detach, ack}, every call deadline-bounded, with TerminalEvent::{Output, Ended, Pong, Idle} - Idle because a quiet terminal is a fact and not a timeout. activate exists because the window size has to reach the terminal BEFORE the program starts; it leaves attach mode for one control exchange and returns, and nothing is lost across the gap because output with nobody attached goes to the ring. PROVEN LIVE, 12 new tests in tests/lifecycle_detached.rs, all macOS: (a) stty size inside the run reports the 40x100 the viewer asked for at attach, and write_input('hello\n') comes back as 'got:hello'; (b) a resize to 50x120 mid-run fires the shell's WINCH trap and the second 'stty size' prints 50 120, which is the SIGWINCH-on-TIOCSWINSZ path proven rather than assumed (the kernel delivers it on a size CHANGE; setting the size a program already has signals nothing, which is why the test changes it); (c) attach/activate/detach/wait 500 ms/reattach is the same session id and the same supervisor pid, the AttachAck reports buffered>0 and dropped=0, and output RESUMES rather than merely replaying; (d) a launcher subprocess prepares interactive-detached, attaches, activates, detaches and exits, and the main process recovers (RecoveryDecision::Attachable), attaches, and sees output still arriving; (e) a run that speaks and finishes while nobody is attached yields AttachAck{state: Exited, exit: Exited{code:0}} then the ring tail then SessionEnded promptly; (f) an Input frame carrying 0xFF, NULs and a well-formed frame header comes back byte-identical through a /bin/cat behind 'stty raw -echo', a malformed tag ends the channel while the session stays reattachable and still talking, and an oversize declared length does the same; (g) a second connection during an attach is told Busy while the attached client is untouched; plus the ring bound, the headless NoTerminal refusal, and the InteractiveNeedsSupervisor refusal on both ephemeral paths. REMOVAL-DETECTED (transcripts in WORKLOG): deleting the unknown-tag guard fails a_tag_this_protocol_does_not_have_is_named_not_skipped AND the live a_frame_tag_this_protocol_does_not_have_ends_the_channel_not_the_run; deleting the scrollback bound fails both ring unit tests (left: 524288, right: 262144) and the live flood test ('the ring must stay bounded: 406282 bytes buffered, bound is 262144'); deleting the EPERM arm from kill_own_group fails a_group_of_zombies_is_nothing_left_to_signal_not_a_refusal on macOS. Pending for R09: re-prepare into an existing session's slot with an incremented generation. Linux verification still blocked (R07): none of the PTY path - open_pty's Linux ptsname_r arm, setsid/TIOCSCTTY, the master's EIO-on-last-slave-close end of file - has been executed on a Linux kernel by this stream.

rows.title: Cleanup verification generation/PID-reuse safe
rows.evidence: Iteration 5 (delta F6): typed CleanupVerification landed (ConfirmedAbsent{basis}/StillPresent{survivors}/Indeterminate{reason}/Unsupported{reason}, closed enum, typed evidence payloads; a sent signal is never a basis). Child leads its own process group (setpgid(0,0) in the trusted pre-exec sequence; failure = typed PreExecStage::ProcessGroup), so a reaped run probes kill(-pgid,0) and an unobserved death probes pid+start_time+boot_id. PID-reuse safe: alive-but-different start time => ConfirmedAbsent{IdentityMismatch}; boot change => ConfirmedAbsent{BootIdChanged} (checked before any probe); unreadable start time => Indeterminate, never a proof of absence; targets <= 1 refused before the syscall. Only ConfirmedAbsent records CleanupConfirmed; duplicate verification refused by the state machine. ActivatedSandbox::stop kills the group (and the child pid, for a setsid escapee) and reports the waitpid observation; StopError::SignalFailed is typed. Live-proven on macOS: verify-after-exit, honest StillPresent for a backgrounded grandchild then ConfirmedAbsent after the consumer kills the group, stop()-then-verify, stopped-before-activation verify; removing setpgid makes the survivor test report ConfirmedAbsent while /bin/sleep 30 still runs. 17 unit + 5 live tests. Iteration 6 (F7) added recovered-session verification: RecoveredSession::verify_cleanup reuses the same verdict machinery over the recorded identity/pgid (DeathObservation::NotReaped, because a recovered process was never waited for by anyone here) and only ConfirmedAbsent marks the record CleanupVerified; ActivatedSandbox::drop now kills the process GROUP before the pid, closing the F6 residual. Pending: Linux verification (R07 blocker); documented dark spot - a descendant that calls setsid leaves the group (needs a cgroup-class mechanism).

rows.title: Machine-readable support report
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) landed lifecycle/support.rs. SupportReport::gather() is infallible and returns a tree of Capability<T> = {status: available|partial|unavailable|unknown, determination: probed_live|platform_api|declared, reason: typed (probed | probe_refused | other_platform | platform_api_linked | not_implemented | not_observable_without_irreversible_change | platform_cannot_express), facts: typed or absent}. NO BARE BOOLEAN anywhere in the serialized tree, locked structurally by a test that walks serde_json::Value and rejects Value::Bool at any depth (removal-detected: adding one bool to CleanupFacts fails 3 tests and prints the JSON pointer). Fields: host (compiled target AND uname(2) sysname/release/version/machine; node name deliberately not read - a hostname is not a capability fact), landlock (REUSES upstream Sandbox::detect_abi + DetectedAbi::has_* for a per-right table filesystem_base/refer/truncate/execute/tcp_network/ioctl_dev/scoping - available only if every right is, else partial; zero diff to sandbox/*), seccomp (upstream's own fork-isolated probe_seccomp_block_network_support -> probed_live), seccomp_user_notification (honestly UNKNOWN: SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER cannot be established without installing a filter that cannot be removed from the installing process, and a kernel release number is not proof since CONFIG_SECCOMP_FILTER can be off), seatbelt (PLATFORM_API not probed_live, with the rationale in reason.why_not_probed: sandbox_init is linked so presence is a compile-time fact, but it applies process-wide and irreversibly, so a live probe must fork - the CLI's setup --check-only does exactly that and is not library machinery; asserted by a macOS test), network_filtering (per-mechanism table incl. seatbelt_per_port_tcp = unavailable/platform_cannot_express naming NetworkFilterUnsupported, so the absence is STATED not inferred), pty (live posix_openpt(O_RDWR|O_NOCTTY) closed immediately -> probed_live) kept SEPARATE from interactive_session (not_implemented) so 'pty: available' cannot be misread as 'the lifecycle will give you one', detached_supervisor + attach (unavailable/not_implemented{R09 slice B} - honest, slice B pending), process_identity (captures THIS process and re-checks: start_time/boot_id/self_recognition all probed_live true on this host), cleanup_verification (signal-0 probes of self and own group, reusing cleanup::{probe_pid,probe_group} made pub(crate) so the report cannot drift from the mechanism), event_observation (per-family fidelity map; kernel_denial = NOT_OBSERVED on BOTH platforms - the lifecycle installs no seccomp-notify listener and macOS Seatbelt denials reach userspace only via the system log; the CLI's log-stream reconstruction is explicitly NOT claimed), dark_spots (typed list of the 4 limits already recorded in module docs: setsid group escape, pgid reuse after reap, exec-or-killed EOF ambiguity, Instant-frozen gate expiry - each with consequence + the file that documents it). Upstream SupportInfo{is_supported} untouched. 17 unit tests + docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md with a golden example locked by a snapshot test that reads the doc itself. macOS values live-verified; the Linux halves (landlock ABI table, seccomp probe) are written-unverified behind the R07 Docker blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) updated two entries: detached_supervisor Unavailable/NotImplemented -> Available/PlatformApi with the supervisor_entry() precondition and its typed failure named in reason.why_not_probed (a probe would have to launch a supervisor); attach Unavailable -> Partial, because control attach landed and terminal attach did not. Both are asserted by their own tests and both are in the golden example locked by docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md. || Iteration 9 (F10) updated two more entries: interactive_session Unavailable/NotImplemented -> Available/PlatformApi, and attach Partial -> Available/PlatformApi. NEITHER became probed_live, and the distinction was kept deliberately: interactive_session takes its STATUS from the live posix_openpt probe (a host that will not give this process a pseudo-terminal cannot run an interactive session however good the supervisor is, and the refusal is then reported with the probe's own reason and its probed_live strength) but NOT its DETERMINATION, because the supervisor half cannot be established without forking twice, execing this binary again, binding a socket and writing a durable record. The live suite tests/lifecycle_detached.rs drives the whole path, but a test that ran on somebody else's machine is not a probe that ran in this process during this call, and probed_live means the latter - claiming it would make the strongest word in this module mean something weaker. attach's why_not_probed states the three limits a consumer must plan around: attach occupies the supervisor's single client slot (a second connection is refused ControlRefusal::Busy), a headless run has no terminal (ControlRefusal::NoTerminal), and scrollback is a bounded ring whose dropped-byte count rides on the next AttachAck. Both entries are asserted by their own tests and both are in the golden example locked by docs/lifecycle/support-report-v1.md.
rows.note: Linux verification BLOCKED pending Docker (see R07). The Linux-only code in support.rs is gather_landlock/gather_seccomp/gather_seccomp_user_notification and the Linux arm of gather_network_filtering; none of it has been executed on a Linux kernel by this stream.

rows.title: Generic event delivery for directly observed events
rows.evidence: Iteration 7 (delta F8) expanded lifecycle/events.rs to the contract shape. LifecycleEvent is now an envelope {session_id: Option<Uuid> (always Some in practice), generation, seq: u64, observed_at: SystemTime captured AT observation, identity: Option<ProcessIdentity>, observation: Observation} around a closed what: LifecycleEventKind {StateChanged (kept, so existing consumers keep their fact), PrepareStarted, SandboxApplied, GateReady, ActivationAttempted{outcome}, Released, ExecObserved, ChildExited{outcome}, StopRequested, StopObserved{outcome}, GateAborted, SupervisorFailure{stage,errno}, CleanupVerdict{verdict}, RecordPersisted{schema_version}}. seq is owned by a crate-internal EventEmitter shared by Arc across the prepared->activated handoff, so one run is ONE unbroken sequence (removal-detected: a second emitter restarts at 0 mid-run and fails both live sequence tests); seq is documented as the ordering authority and observed_at explicitly is NOT (a wall clock can step). ActivationOutcome = {Accepted, RefusedWrongSession, RefusedWrongGeneration, RefusedGateClosed{state}, RefusedExpired, RefusedInvalidToken} carries NO token material by construction, locked by a test that walks the serialized tree rejecting any key named token/nonce/secret/digest and ANY array (every secret in the module is a [u8; N]) plus a long-blob check over serde and Debug (removal-detected). No synthesized kernel denials: the vocabulary has no variant for what the platform does not show. Emission points: prepare() -> PrepareStarted (pre-fork, the one event with no identity); the child's gate-ready record -> SandboxApplied + GateReady; activate() -> ActivationAttempted at every outcome, Released after the claim's write, ExecObserved on EOF; wait() -> ChildExited; stop paths -> StopRequested/StopObserved; abort_gate -> GateAborted (only when a live gate was closed); fail_activation -> SupervisorFailure; verify_cleanup -> CleanupVerdict for EVERY verdict, not only ConfirmedAbsent; SessionStore write -> RecordPersisted (never for a write that failed). Every emit is outside the SharedLifecycle lock and after the fact; SessionHandle::persist was restructured to release the record mutex BEFORE calling the sink, so consumer code never runs under a library lock. Rule the order follows: the fact first, then the state change it caused. Proven: 8 new unit tests + 3 live (whole-vocabulary happy run, stopped run reported as stop_requested/stop_observed rather than child_exited, refused activation carrying no token material), each live test asserting the exact sequence, seq gaplessness, observed_at non-decreasing, and identity present on every event after the fork. docs/lifecycle/lifecycle-event-v1.md carries the field table and a golden example locked by a snapshot test. macOS live-verified; the Linux halves are the same code paths behind the R07 blocker. || Iteration 8 (F9) added the honest answer to 'what happens to events when there is no caller'. EventSink stays caller-side and NOTHING was invented to deliver events to a caller that is not there: a detached supervisor installs its own EventRing sink and persists the last DETACHED_EVENT_RING_CAPACITY = 32 events into the session record (schema v2 field), oldest dropped, read back by DetachedSession::status().events(). The fidelity is documented as bounded and lossy in three places (the constant, the record schema doc, and the client module). The one event a supervisor learns about rather than witnesses - a child that ended at the gate while nobody asked - is emitted with Observation::Reconstructed, as is the PrepareStarted of an adopted child, whose fork happened in the launcher before the supervisor image existed.
rows.note: API shape change for consumers: LifecycleEvent went from enum to struct. LifecycleEvent::StateChanged{from,to,observation} is now LifecycleEventKind::StateChanged{from,to} reached via event.what(), with observation on the envelope. Recorded in HANDOFF.md.
